If helpful, we can accept the usual infringement exclusions (our modifications, combinations or specifications) plus procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x annual fees cap on Licensor's indemnity.

proposal.summary: Add a Licensor indemnity (IP infringement, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) and narrow the Licensee indemnity to Licensee-provided content and Licensee's breach of law.

quote: ARTICLE XII INDEMNITY Licensee will be solely responsible for any commercial or legal liability that may arise as a result of Licensee's exercise of any of the license rights granted by Licensor to Licensee under this Agreement, and Licensee shall defend, indemnify, and hold Licensor harmless from and against any and all suits, claims, proceedings, judgments, awards, damages, loss, liability, cost and expenses
rationale: Article XII is a one-way indemnity running from Licensee to Licensor, and it is drafted very broadly (Licensee's exercise of the license, conduct of its business, any breach). There is no Licensor indemnity anywhere in the Agreement, and Article XIII(a) goes further by excluding all Licensor liability for claims that use of the Licensed Technology infringes third-party IP, while Article XIII(b) caps Licensor liability at one half of fees paid. That is the playbook walk-away position: no Vendor IP indemnity plus a one-way Customer indemnity. The redline inserts a Licensor defence and indemnity for IP infringement, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, disapplies the Article XIII limitations to that indemnity (otherwise it is illusory), and narrows our indemnity to Licensee-provided content and our own breach of applicable law.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article III gives Licensor ownership of everything, including the customisation work we commission and pay for under Article VII(b), and says nothing about our own trading, order and client data. We have added a short carve-out so that we own custom deliverables we pay for (with Licensor keeping its pre-existing platform IP subject to a perpetual, royalty-free licence back to us), we retain all rights in our data, and nothing is jointly owned. If Licensor must retain title to customisation embedded in the Platform, we can instead accept a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense those deliverables for our business, but the data-ownership sentence is required.

ops.text: Notwithstanding the foregoing: (i) Licensor hereby assigns to Licensee all right, title and interest in and to any deliverables, work product and materials developed specifically for Licensee and paid for by Licensee, including the unique client front end and other customization work described in Article VII(b) (the "Custom Deliverables"), excluding Licensor's pre-existing Intellectual Property Rights embedded therein, as to which Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free and fully paid-up license to use, modify and sublicense such Intellectual Property Rights solely as embedded in the Custom Deliverables for Licensee's business purposes; (ii) Licensee retains all right, title and interest in and to all data, records and information provided, submitted or generated by or on behalf of Licensee or its clients in connection with the Licensed Technology, including trade, order and client data ("Licensee Data"), and nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to Licensor any Licensee Data or any Intellectual Property Rights of Licensee; and (iii) no deliverable, work product or other material created under this Agreement shall be jointly owned by the parties.

proposal.summary: Add customer-side ownership carve-outs to Article III: Licensor assigns custom deliverables paid for by Licensee (with licence-back of embedded Licensor IP), Licensee retains all rights in its data, and no joint ownership.

quote: ARTICLE III OWNERSHIP Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein.
rationale: Article III (p0048) gives Licensor ownership of the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein, and "Derivative Work" (p0005) sweeps in any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements based on the Licensed Technology — which captures the bespoke "unique client front end and other enhancements" that we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) (p0087). Our only rights are the restricted, non-exclusive, Field-of-Use licence, with all other rights expressly reserved to Licensor (p0043), so we would pay for custom deliverables and receive no ownership and no perpetual licence back. The Agreement is also silent on our data: there is no provision confirming that our trading, order and client data and records remain ours, while "Intellectual Property Rights" is defined solely as rights "of Licensor" (p0008) and Confidential Information (p0004) is defined one-way in Licensor's favour. Licensor's ownership of its platform is acceptable, but the playbook requires that we own (or at minimum hold a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to) deliverables created for us, that we retain all rights in our data, and that nothing is jointly owned. The proposed insertion after p0048 is the minimal fix and preserves Licensor's pre-existing platform IP.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have made the damages exclusion and the liability cap mutual and reset the cap to the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000; as drafted only Licensor was capped (at one half of amounts paid) while Licensee's exposure was unlimited. Indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and Licensee's fee obligations are not counted against it; a mutual cap of 12 months' fees with at least those carve-outs is our fallback.

ops.oldText: (a) IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE TO LICENSEE OR TO ANY THIRD PARTY FOR ANY SPECIAL, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES

ops.newText: (b) EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (i) THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY LICENSEE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (ii) USD 1,000,000. proposal.summary: Make Article XIII exclusion and cap mutual, reset cap to greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, and add uncapped Excluded Claims

quote: (b) IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED ONE HALF OF THE AMOUNT PAID BY THE LICENSEE TO Licensor HEREUNDER.
rationale: Article XIII is entirely one-sided: only Licensor benefits from the consequential-damages exclusion, and only Licensor's aggregate liability is capped — at one half of amounts paid, which is far below the walk-away floor of six months' fees, while our client's liability (including the broad Article XII indemnity) remains unlimited. There are no carve-outs for confidentiality, data/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement. The redline makes both the exclusion and the cap mutual, sets the cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, adds uncapped Excluded Claims, and confirms Licensee's fee obligations are not damages for cap purposes.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need a carve-out allowing assignment to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, with any other assignment consent applied mutually and not unreasonably withheld, and we cannot accept automatic termination of our licenses (or a consent/competitor veto) on our own change of control. If helpful, we can accept a fallback of mutual assignment to successors on written notice with consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.

proposal.summary: Add affiliate/successor assignment carve-out for Licensee, make consent standard mutual and reasonable, and remove Licensor's automatic termination right on Licensee's change of control.

quote: (c) ASSIGNMENT. Licensee may not assign this Agreement or assign, sublicense and/or transfer in any manner its license rights hereunder in whole or in part without Licensor's prior written consent.
rationale: The assignment clause is one-sided and at the playbook's walk-away threshold: it bars Licensee (our client) from any assignment without Licensor's consent, with no affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard, while imposing no restriction on Licensor (including no bar on assignment to a Licensee competitor). Worse, Article XX(a) provides that our licenses automatically terminate on any Change of Control of Licensee unless Licensor consents in advance, and Licensor is deemed reasonable in refusing where the acquirer is competitive with Licensor or where Licensor merely believes its interests would be adversely affected — an effective veto and termination right over our own M&A. The redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out, makes the consent requirement mutual and subject to a reasonableness standard, bars Licensor assignment to our competitors, and removes the change-of-control termination/consent/re-pricing right.

quote: Licensee acknowledges that the grant of the license set forth in this Section is a non-exclusive license and that the Licensor shall have the right to use and to license to other parties the Licensed Technology for any purpose and in any manner as Licensor may determine in its sole discretion.
rationale: No exclusive-dealing, sole-supplier or requirements obligation is imposed on us. The grant is expressly non-exclusive in both directions (p0001, p0030, p0043, p0049), and the license restrictions in Article II (p0035–p0047) and the sub-license bar in Article VI (p0085) only limit how we may use or transfer Licensor's own Licensed Technology; they do not restrict us from licensing or using competing FX platforms or from procuring services from other providers. There is no "sole and exclusive provider", "all of its requirements" or "shall not procure from any third party" language anywhere in the Agreement, and the only exclusivity-flavoured constraints on us relate to Field of Use scope (p0007) rather than sourcing freedom. The Article XXII "Right of First Refusal" (p0139) is a first-look right over a sale/merger of Licensee, i.e. a change-of-control restriction, not an exclusivity or purchasing covenant, so it falls outside this rule (it may warrant review under the change-of-control/assignment rule). Accordingly the EXCLUSIVITY preferred position is met and no redline is needed.

The fee provisions (Art. V and the Monthly Notional Volume tiers, p0056-p0070) are purely usage-based per-trade fees plus a $2,500/month support fee (p0086); the only "in no event less than" floor in p0070 is (as drafted) directed at the Licensor and in any event is a true-up to actual recorded trade volume rather than a stipulated damages amount. Termination provisions (Art. IV p0049, Art. XXI p0138) impose no exit payment — Licensor merely retains the right to be paid for trades already performed — and Art. XXIII expressly bars termination damages against either party. Audit cost-shifting on a >5% discrepancy (p0064) is an audit-cost allocation, not a Customer-payable penalty, and falls outside this rule. The rebate/share arrangements (p0075-p0076) run in our favour. No redline required.

Licensor hereby, subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement and provided that Licensee makes payments to Licensor as required under this Agreement, grants to Licensee a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use and subject to the additional restrictions set forth below and otherwise in this License Agreement.

This falls short of the playbook preferred position (affiliates and contractors covered, termination only for uncured material breach, transferable to successors). The redline amends the grant paragraph to add Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (with our continuing responsibility for their compliance), confirm successor transferability, and limit termination to a material breach uncured after 30 days' notice, overriding the conflicting restrictions.

quote: iii. Licensor hereby, subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement and provided that Licensee makes payments to Licensor as required under this Agreement, grants to Licensee a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use and subject to the additional restrictions set forth below and otherwise in this License Agreement.
rationale: No non-compete or competing-products covenant binds us. Every restriction imposed on the Licensee is a scope-of-licence or IP-protection limit on use of the Licensor's own Licensed Technology, not a restraint on our business: the "Field of Use" definition (p0007) and grant (p0030) limit only how we may use the Platform; the "Additional Restrictions" (p0035, p0040-p0047, incl. the derivative-works bar at p0044) and the sub-licence bar (p0085) restrict only dealings in the Licensed Technology. Nothing prevents us from operating any business, licensing or building a competing FX platform, or trading through other venues or ECNs, and there is no exclusivity, minimum-volume or territory covenant (fees are volume-based only). The three-year post-term non-solicit (p0125) restricts hiring, not competition, and the Change of Control consent/competitor test (p0134) and Right of First Refusal (p0139) are assignment/exit controls — all reviewed under their own playbook rules, not NONCOMPETE. A field-of-use limit on the vendor's licensed software is the core priced bargain here, so deleting it would be disproportionate under this rule and is not the restraint this rule targets. Compliant with the preferred position; no redline proposed.

rationale: Article IV commits Licensee to a 36-month Initial Period, and no provision anywhere in the Agreement (Articles IV, XIX, XX, XXI) gives Licensee any right to terminate without cause; termination rights run almost entirely in Licensor's favour (immediate termination on any Licensee breach, Change of Control, wind-up), and Licensor also controls renewal. Absence of a Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation under T4C. We therefore insert a Licensee termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirm Licensor has no convenience exit mid-term. ops.newText: Any such audit shall be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice from Licensor, during Licensee's normal business hours, and by an auditor bound by written obligations of confidentiality no less protective than those set forth in this Agreement. Any such audit shall be limited to the accounting records described above, which Licensee may make available off-site, and shall not include access to Licensee's systems, networks or facilities.

quote: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
rationale: Article II §IV(b) binds Licensee (our client) to permit audits of its accounting records. The clause satisfies parts of the playbook position — the auditor must be an independent CPA/audit professional selected by mutual agreement, and p0064 already allocates audit cost to Licensor unless a discrepancy exceeding 5% is found — but it contains no frequency cap (audits could be demanded repeatedly), gives no advance notice (the 30-day period is our compliance deadline after a request, not prior notice), and does not limit the audit to business hours, bind the auditor to confidentiality, or confine the review to records provided off-site. Redline inserts once-per-12-months, 30 days' prior written notice, business hours, auditor confidentiality, and no access to our systems or facilities; cost allocation is left as-is since it already meets the preferred 5% threshold.

quote: the validity, interpretation and legal effect of this Agreement shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of New York, U.S.A., applicable to contracts entered in and performed entirely within the State of New York, U.S.A. without regard to any conflict of law principles.
rationale: The General Provisions governing-law clause selects internal New York law (p0145) and requires all suits to be instituted in the City of New York with irrevocable submission to the exclusive jurisdiction of the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York or the New York state courts, plus waiver of venue and forum non conveniens objections (p0146). That is our preferred position: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction of state and federal courts sitting in New York. A document-wide search returns no arbitration provision and no other dispute-resolution forum, so there is no offshore arbitration seat or foreign venue risk. No redline needed.

quote: (b) The Licensee shall calculate the license fee payable to the Licensor for each month based on the Monthly Notional Volume bands for that pay period and shall pay the Licensor accordingly. In no event shall the amount payable by the Licensor be less than the amount recorded by the Licensee as being traded with the Licensed Technology multiplied by the applicable Fees set forth above.
rationale: The fee construct in Article V is purely usage-based: the US$7.50–US$5.00 per US$1 million tiers are volume discounts, and the highest band reached simply sets the blended rate (p0067). There is no committed floor, minimum notional volume, take-or-pay, or shortfall/penalty mechanic anywhere in the Agreement (searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall" return nothing relevant), and the only fixed charges are the $35,000 initial payment already advanced and the $2,500/month technical support fee for services actually provided — i.e., usage or ordered services only. The "in no event ... less than" language in p0070 is a floor keyed to trades actually recorded as executed on the platform, not a committed volume. The volume-based rebate in p0076 runs in our favour (Licensor pays us). This meets the preferred position, so no redline is proposed.

rationale: Article IV grants Licensor a unilateral option to extend the 36-month Initial Period by a further seven years, with no Licensee consent right, no non-renewal notice mechanism and no limit on fee increases for the extension period. A Licensor-controlled multi-year renewal is a walk-away item under the playbook and is inconsistent with clauses II and III of the same Article, which contemplate extension only by mutual written agreement. The redline sets renewal to mutual written 12-month increments, requires 60 days' notice of renewal and any fee change, and caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3%; fallback is 12-month automatic renewal with a 30-day (max 60-day) opt-out and a 5% cap.

proposal.summary: Insert Licensor transition-assistance, data-return and deletion-certification obligations into Article XXI (Effect of Termination)

quote: ARTICLE XXI EFFECT OF TERMINATION Upon termination of this Agreement: for any reason (a) the rights and licenses granted to Licensee pursuant to this Agreement will automatically terminate, and (b) Licensee shall, within five (5) days, ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation with respect to the Licensed Technology and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control
rationale: The Agreement contains no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation on Licensor. Article XXI (Effect of Termination) runs one way only: licenses terminate immediately and Licensee must ship all Licensor materials back within five days and certify compliance, with all Licensor rights surviving. Searches for "return", "data", "transition" and "terminat" surface no export, retrieval, migration or deletion-certification duty for Licensor, and the confidentiality article (p0124) likewise binds only Licensee. Because this is a hosted FX trading platform where our trade and account records reside on Licensor's systems, silence leaves us exposed to loss of our own data on exit (the walk-away outcome). Inserted a new Article XXI(c) tracking the playbook preferred position: up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return of Licensee Data within 30 days, and deletion with written certification thereafter; the 90-day fallback is flagged in the comment.

quote: THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY IS PROVIDED ON AN "AS IS" BASIS WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND AND LICENSOR HEREBY
rationale: Article VIX is a pure disclaimer: the Licensed Technology is provided "AS IS", all express and implied warranties (merchantability, non-infringement, fitness, title, accuracy) are disclaimed, and Licensor expressly does not warrant that the technology is error-free, will meet Licensee's requirements, or that nonconformities to the Documentation will be corrected. A search of the Agreement shows no affirmative Licensor performance or conformance warranty anywhere; the only "warrants" language runs against Licensee or is mutual boilerplate about counsel. This is the walk-away position under the WARRANTY rule, so we insert an express warranty (workmanlike services, 12-month conformance of the Licensed Software to the Documentation, compliance with laws, no malicious code) with a repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy, and carve it out of the disclaimer so the disclaimer does not swallow it. Fallback of 90 days/30 days is available.

rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance clause: the outline has no insurance heading and the only occurrence of "insurance" is in the fees paragraph (p0051) allocating taxes, customs, duties, insurance and shipping to Licensee.
